'''Chicken and andouille sausage gumbo''' is a soup or[[Cookbook:Stews | stew]] which is is prepared using[[Cookbook:Roux | roux]].

== Ingredients ==
* about 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]]
* 1 cup (240 g) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Bell pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] into ¼-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] pieces
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], chopped into ¼-inch pieces
* 4 stalks of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], chopped into ¼-inch pieces
* [[Cookbook:Chicken Stock|Chicken stock]] or equivalent
* about ½ lb (¼ kg) Andouille [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]] or other spicy sausage
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper |Cayenne pepper]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Salt |Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==
# Brown outside of chicken breasts in small amount of oil then set aside.
# Make a [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]] from the flour in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# Add peppers, onions, and celery to roux. Cook until softened.
# Slowly stir in water, and bring to a simmer.
# Cut up browned chicken breasts, add to gumbo, and cook until done.
# Slice up sausage and add ½ hour after the chicken.
# Season to taste with cayenne and salt.
# Serve in a bowl with a little rice and green onions on top.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Hot sauce can be added to taste.
*[[Cookbook:Filé|Filé]] may be added to thicken individual servings as served.
*Home-made chicken stock is preferable to store-bought.
*Gumbo will be better if left over night and eaten the next day.
